newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Asian jibe hurts Australian trade - farmers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Asian jibe hurts Australian trade - farmers.

text.p: Australian farm leader Ian Macfarlane said on Thursday an independent politician's "racist" remarks about Asian immigration were threatening Australian trade with the region.

"Her comments regarding Asian immigration, and the basic racist undertones associated with them, are causing a great deal of offence, alarm and instability amongst our Asian business trading partners," the Queensland Grain Growers Association president told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
In September, lower house member Pauline Hanson called on the government to stop Asian immigration and foreign aid.
Macfarlane warned that Hanson's comments could undermine Australia's lucrative farm exports to key markets such as Japan, China, Indonesia and South Korea, worth billions of dollars a year.

"We don't want to see those regions put at risk and those markets into those regions put at risk by the failure of the prime minister (John Howard) and other senior government officials to challenge and disassociate ourselves from some of the comments that have been made," he said.

"The comments have caused offence and they've caused a degree of uncertainty amongst both the Asian-based community here and that business community ... and their contacts in both south-east Asia and the biggest Asian region."
Howard earlier this week said some of Hanson's comments reflected a singificant part of the Australian community.
But his deputy and trade minister, Tim Fischer, has also warned Hanson's comments could damage trade.
Macfarlane urged Howard to publicly repudiate Hanson.
"We need to obviously give a clear message to re-cement our relationship with the business and community leaders in that region," he said.

"These comments are being widely reported in south-east Asia, the fact that they haven't been challenged by the prime minister is also being reported, the fact that this whole issue appears to be gaining some groundswell and momentum in Australia is causing alarm amongst our trading partners in south-east Asia..."
